text:
Anna (Support): Customer reports promo TRYRED-2026 is rejected as 'promo_not_available_in_region' even though dashboard shows it active globally. Customer email: anna.customer@example.com. Case #CS-2309
Rebecca (Support): thanks — can you paste the exact API call they ran and the response body?
Anna (Support): here's what the customer sent (redacted):
```
POST /v1/claims
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk-live-***
Content-Type: application/json
{
  \"org_id\": \"org_83x7\",
  \"user_email\": \"anna.customer@example.com\",
  \"promo_code\": \"TRYRED-2026\"
}
```
Response: 403 {"error":"promo_not_available_in_region", "promo":"TRYRED-2026"} (customer is in IE, dashboard shows country: ALL)
Kyle (Eng): tagging me. quick Q: did customer include X-Forwarded-For or any region header? sometimes our geo path falls back to IP.
Anna (Support): they didn't add any special headers, just the SDK call through browser.
Maya (Payments): I pulled the promo record from the promo-service DB for TRYRED-2026:
```
promo_id: promo_9021
code: TRYRED-2026
status: active
allowed_regions: []
created_by: growth@redwood.ai
type: global_v1
```
Note: allowed_regions is an empty array. older promos used null for global, new migration left [] which our new policy handler treats as empty-allowlist -> deny.
Kyle (Eng): ahh that explains it. behavior change during promo-schema migration: empty array now means 'no regions' instead of 'global'. we updated the region-checker to treat null as global but not [].
Rebecca (Support): ok can we confirm repro in staging?
Kyle (Eng): repro steps (staging):
1) create promo via promo-service with allowed_regions: []
2) run claim against any EU IP
```
POST /staging/v1/claims
{
  \"org_id\": \"org-test\",
  \"promo_code\": \"TRYRED-2026\"
}
```
Response: 403 promo_not_available_in_region
Kyle (Eng): logs (claim-service):
```
[2026-03-17T15:24:12Z] claim_request id=clm_xxx org=org-test code=TRYRED-2026
[2026-03-17T15:24:12Z] promo_lookup id=promo_9021 allowed_regions=[]
[2026-03-17T15:24:12Z] region_check FAIL detected_region=IE allowed=[] -> DENY
```
Jordan (Billing): customer wants credits immediately. I can push a manual credit to org_83x7 once we have approval to do so.
Maya (Payments): short-term mitigation: we can treat empty array as global in runtime until migration fix lands. long-term: backfill promos where allowed_regions is [] -> null for global_v1 promos.
Kyle (Eng): I'll open a PR to treat [] as global for legacy promo type and add a backfill job. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/promo-service/pull/482
infra-bot: deploy queued for promo-service: deploy/ci-2026-03-17-482 -> staging
Kyle (Eng): plan: 1) apply hotfix (treat [] as legacy-global) -> quick deploy to staging, smoke test 2) run backfill to convert [] -> null for impacted promos 3) deploy safe migration for prod next window.
Rebecca (Support): Jordan, can you grant a one-off credit and let customer know it's applied? I'll follow up once migration is done.
Jordan (Billing): done, granted 50 credits to org_83x7 and emailed customer. internal note #BILL-1147.
Maya (Payments): I've scheduled the backfill job for tonight 02:00 UTC and added a data migration script.
Kyle (Eng): hotfix merged and promoted to prod after quick QA. PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/promo-service/pull/482#commit
Rebecca (Support): customer confirmed code now accepted after credits + fix, thanks team :thumbsup:
Anna (Support): closing case CS-2309 after customer ack.
Kyle (Eng): follow-up: we'll add a metric to detect promos with empty allowed_regions so this doesn't regress. created ticket INF-912.
